Remaining for full scope: A depth-resolved conduction model needs conductivity, density, heat capacity, layered material / ice, spin-up and surface boundary history. EMARS surface temperature is available but does not supply temperatures at depth.

Geometric visibility is implemented. A communication schedule still needs operational pass allocations plus antenna attitudes, radio compatibility, link budgets and local terrain. NASA MaROS supplies operational planning, but a public machine-readable schedule feed was not verified in this audit.

Environmental grids and local measurements exist. Route integration needs arrival times, stops and return travel plus validated UV / dose / thermal-response fields and suit assumptions. Unsupported route intervals must stay unknown rather than contribute zero exposure.

Terrain walking cost is already available. Time-dependent energy needs separately validated metabolic, suit life-support / thermal or vehicle models with mass, speed, stops, battery state and weather. Climate temperature alone cannot determine energy use.

Historical observed masks are connected. A current storm perimeter would require newly published masks or a validated detection pipeline on timestamped MARCI images; climate dust optical depth is not a storm polygon.

REMS instrument-band history is connected. A current global 315–400 nm field needs spectral radiative transfer, aerosols, solar geometry and a defined receiver geometry, validated against REMS / MEDA bands.

REMS 220–280 nm history is connected locally. A global sub-280 nm surface field needs spectral solar input and CO₂ / ozone / aerosol transmission. Missing short-wavelength coverage cannot be assumed zero.

MEDA RDS has calibrated local spectral and broadband solar measurements. A 400–700 nm global surface field needs a specified band / geometry and validated spectral integration. A narrow detector band or 0.2–1.2 μm panchromatic channel is not the full visible band. MEDA archive decoding is additional engineering, not missing data.

Define the solar-IR wavelength interval first. MEDA TIRS measures reflected shortwave 0.3–3 μm and thermal longwave, which are not an isolated downward solar-IR band. Archive products exist; global solar-IR requires spectral separation / transfer.

Requires dated magnetic-field / solar-wind solutions and field-line tracing to Mars, with source-surface / transport assumptions. Existing Earth-L1 IMF values cannot determine Mars connectivity. A Parker-spiral approximation would need explicit limitations and validation.

Historical RAD dose / particle responses and published GCR models exist. A dated modulation potential or species-resolved boundary spectrum needs calibration, radial transport assumptions and uncertainty; Earth F10.7 is context, not a modulation potential.

The verified iPATH feed has deterministic forecast issues, not calibrated probability intervals. Supply an ensemble or a hindcast / observed-event calibration with coverage tests. Revisions between runs cannot be labelled confidence bounds.
